subject: Capacity true-up / one-off settlement for Jun–Aug burst
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@novushealth.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novushealth.com
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected Jun–Aug burst — request for reconciliation and one-off settlement

Hi Michael,

Hope you're well. During our June–August pilot we saw multiple sustained bursts above our committed Dedicated capacity which produced unexpected overages on the Aug invoice. Procurement asked me to reach out to reconcile the retroactive usage and discuss a one-off settlement — ideally a single line invoice or credit so we can close this quarter's books.

I've attached a CSV export from our monitoring showing hourly peak GPU minutes for Jun 1–Aug 31 and the billing CSV from our portal. Key callouts:
- Week of Jul 12–18: sustained 2.8x peak for 48 hours (migration testing)
- Aug 3–9: multiple short bursts that spiked billable tokens and GPU minutes

Can Redwood provide a reconciliation with the committed capacity baseline and proposed charged amount, and confirm whether a one-time invoice or applied credit is possible? Procurement would prefer an invoice they can route for approval.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Director, Cloud Operations
Novus Health

Attachments: Novus_Usage_Jun-Aug-2026.csv, billing-export-Aug.csv
From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rossi <elena@novushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Jun–Aug burst — request for reconciliation and one-off settlement

Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed export and the heads-up. Looping in Marissa (finance) and Vivek (AE) so we can get a settlement path in motion.

Action plan from our side:
1) Marissa will run a line-by-line reconciliation against your committed capacity and our billing records and produce a short reconciliation statement (expected 2 business days).
2) We will present two remediation options: a) one-time invoice for overage (procurement-friendly) or b) applied credit against next renewal.
3) If procurement requires a signed amendment for the additional one-off charge, I can prepare a one-page amendment and send via DocuSign.

Couple of clarifying questions to speed this up:
- Which billing contact should the invoice be addressed to (name + PO if applicable)?
- Are any of the burst periods already part of a technical dispute with your engineering team?

Vivek — any constraints on offering a partial goodwill credit for the Aug migration spike?

Elena — I'll target sending the reconciliation and recommended invoice by EOD Wed (2026-08-18).

Best,
Michael Grant
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena@novushealth.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novushealth.com

Novus Health 
AP Invoices

ap.invoices@novushealth.com

Engineering confirms the Jul 12–18 migration was internal and they accept the usage; the Aug 3–9 bursts were triggered by an integration test that should have run in a sandbox — we are still investigating root cause. Procurement would still prefer a one-time invoice to process this round.

If you can provide an invoice description line that explains the period and reason (e.g., "Retroactive capacity true-up for sustained burst usage during Jun–Aug 2026"), that will help approvals.

Elena

Attachments: usage-sample-screenshots.zip
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T09:43:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Proposed reconciliation and settlement options (Novus)

Folks — I ran the numbers against the committed capacity and the recorded billable GPU minutes/tokens. Summary below (rounded):

Committed monthly capacity (Jul & Aug averaged): 12,000 GPU-min/month equivalent
Billed usage (Jun–Aug window apportioned to months):
- Jun: 11,200 (within commit)
- Jul: 18,900 (overage ~6,900)
- Aug: 15,500 (overage ~3,500)

Rate: $0.65 / GPU-min equivalent (account standard rate)
Raw overage charge: (6,900 + 3,500) * $0.65 = $6,885 (rounded $6,900)

Goodwill options to propose:
A) Full one-time invoice for $6,900 (procurement-preferred)
B) One-time invoice for $5,520 (20% goodwill credit applied)
C) Apply $3,450 credit to next renewal + invoice $3,450 for remainder

Recommendation: Offer B as the default (20% courtesy on the migration spike), but make C available if they want to keep next quarter billing simpler. If procurement insists on an invoice to close their books, we send option B with an itemized line and DocuSign-ready amendment.

I have prepared a draft invoice and a short amendment PDF (attached). If Vivek signs off, I'll route the DocuSign.

Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_Invoice_Novus_OneOff.xlsx, Draft_Amendment_NVH_Docusign.pdf
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Proposed reconciliation and settlement options (Novus)

Thanks Marissa — I approve option B (20% goodwill). Rationale: keeps procurement happy, preserves the renewal economics, and acknowledges the migration disruption without setting a broad precedent.

Marissa — please send the invoice to ap.invoices@novushealth.com with PO-4492-2026 and route the DocuSign amendment to Elena. Michael — offer a 7-day window for payment before we apply to next renewal if they prefer credit.

Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
